objective: Settle the AppImage discovery roots before anything is cut: an unset `AppImageInstallPath` must reach the AppImages that exist, or deleting `sync_appimages()` freezes the metadata database and the Python stays the only writer that ever saw this machine's AppImages (F11).

red_test_first.test: Calix.Cli.Zig/src/commands/sync.zig::real AppImage runner discovers an AppImage in the applications directory with no install path configured
red_test_first.failed_because: expected 1, found 0 -- the runner returned early on `~/.local/bin` not existing, and would have scanned only that directory if it had existed
red_test_first.note: The test deliberately does not create `~/.local/bin`, because a machine without it would otherwise never scan at all.

changes.Calix.Cli.Zig/src/runtime/xdg.zig: `applicationsDirectory()` -- `~/Applications`, derived from the invoking user's home and not from `XDG_BIN_HOME`, because it is the AppImage convention the architecture document and the Python script share, not an XDG directory.
changes.Calix.PackageManager/src/appimage/discov: `Options.install_directory` becomes `install_directories`: `discover` reads the desktop entries once and scans every root, skipping a root that is absent instead of treating it as 'nothing to find'.
changes.Calix.PackageManager/src/appimage/manage: `discoverAppImages(install_directories, applications_directory)` -- the roots are the caller's decision; the backend still knows only the directory AppImages are installed into.
changes.Calix.Cli.Zig/src/commands/sync.zig: `discoveryRoots()` returns the configured install directory (or its `~/.local/bin` default) followed by `~/Applications`, deduplicated; `anyRootExists()` replaces the single-directory early return; the two messages now name every root.

defects_found_while_making_it_pass.buildAppImage leaked every derived strin: name, version, icon, description, the inner `v{version}` tag source and the joined AppImage path were allocated and only released on the error path, so a successful scan leaked six allocations per AppImage. Nothing had ever called `discover` on real files, so the leak had never been observed. Fixed with an arena for the scratch values and a `defer` on the joined path.
defects_found_while_making_it_pass.buildAppImage aliased its own fields: `.desktop_name` was set to the same pointer as `.name`, while `freeAppImage` frees both -- the first caller to free a discovered record would free one allocation twice. It is now its own copy.
defects_found_while_making_it_pass.merge degraded `release_tag`: The scan derives a tag from the version it sees; when the filename fallback yields `1.0.0` the tag became `v1.0.0` while the database's `0.11.1` version was kept, so the record said two different versions. `releaseTagMatches` uses the tag to suppress an update the machine already has, so the pair being inconsistent means a false update. The tag now travels with the version it names. Found by case G on the host's own data (EffectCraft's desktop entry carries no `X-AppImage-Version`).

proofs.reproducer: .ci-cache/proof/s1-roots-proof.sh (ignored scratch; the log is the durable record)
proofs.A: AppImageInstallPath unset, `~/.local/bin` absent, one AppImage in `~/Applications` -> exit 0, one record carrying name, version, icon and description from the desktop entry, and the message names both roots
proofs.B: a record at /opt/Ghost.AppImage added by hand -> still there after the scan (the merge keeps what it does not see)
proofs.C: AppImageInstallPath set, one AppImage in each root -> two records, both roots scanned
proofs.D: AppImageInstallPath naming `~/Applications` -> one root, no duplicate record
proofs.F: the host's AppImages with no database at all -> 15 records rebuilt from `~/Applications`; 14 identical to the live database, EffectCraft's version falling back to `1.0.0` because its desktop entry carries none
proofs.G: the host's AppImages scanned on top of a copy of the live database -> 15 records before, 15 after, 15/15 identical record for record
proofs.E: the host read only: AppImageInstallPath null, 0 AppImages in `~/.local/bin`, 15 in `~/Applications`, 15 database records, all under `~/Applications`
proofs.gate: `./scripts/verify --quick` PASSED on a dirty tree -- cli 414 tests, package manager 1392, ui 259; record ~/.local/state/calix/verify/local-verify-20261028T184246Z/run.json
proofs.log_source: Regenerated from the release build of commit 72c9f659, not from the working tree that produced it: the log's timestamp line is the only thing that differs from the run that guided the fix.

message_change.what: `Discovered {d} AppImage(s) in {dir}.` became `Tracking {d} AppImage(s); scanned {dir, dir}.`
message_change.why: The count is the number of records the database holds after the merge, not the number the scan found, and there is no longer one directory to name. `No AppImage directory exists ({roots}). No AppImages to sync.` replaces the single-directory sentence for the same reason.
message_change.test_updated: `real AppImage runner reports a missing install directory without failing` now asserts the two halves of the new sentence instead of the old one.

what_this_does_not_do.write_default_unchanged: `install`, `list`, `list-updates`, `upgrade` and the daemon still fall back to `~/.local/bin` when `AppImageInstallPath` is unset. Only discovery was widened, because only discovery decides what enters the database; changing where installs land is a narrower, separate decision.
what_this_does_not_do.run_and_remove_still_look_in_two_places: `remove` and `run` search the configured directory and the `~/.local/bin` fallback, and fall back to the database name on a miss (remove) or fail (run). On this machine, with the setting unset, `calix run appimage` therefore still cannot find an AppImage in `~/Applications`. That is the remaining half of F11.
what_this_does_not_do.python_writer_alive: `sync_appimages()` still runs on the 4-hourly timer. Step 8 deletes it, in the same commit as the root it no longer has to supply.
what_this_does_not_do.no_deployment: No unit changed and nothing was installed on the host; the host was only read.

next: S1 step 8: delete `sync_appimages()` -- the root it supplied is now the backend's own -- then commit b (schema 2, the worker thread, the registry merged into one document, the Python release writer cut).
